as_told.title: Alcubierre warp drive and Sonny White's Casimir chip
as_told.place_text: National Autonomous University of Mexico; NASA

plain: The claim is that in 1994 a Mexican physics student named Miguel Alcubierre showed that faster-than-light travel is possible in theory under Einstein's own equations. A man named Karl Nell tells it on the show. He says Alcubierre, then a postgraduate at the University of Mexico, "solved Einstein's equations for an effective faster than light mechanism." Michels raises it on two later episodes. He notes that the proof only works "if you do have negative energy," and he pairs it with a chip that a NASA engineer, Harold "Sonny" White, built around the Casimir effect, a tiny force that appears between very close metal plates. The point is that real physics may allow the kind of travel reported for UFOs.
